_doc: T-194 (UPDATE 11 'LAZARUS', work order §5; shot lists docs/CUTSCENES_LAZARUS.md, T-191): the four LAZARUS cutscenes and the Moscow 1953 card, in the campaign.json `cutscenes` shape so CinemaDirector.validate and the clip tool read them unchanged. A shot adds `_set` (its stage: `sets`), `_what` (the shot list's 'what is seen'), `fx` / `fx_at` (the stage's effects), `lines` ([[t, id]]), `squad_lines` ([[t, seat, suffix]]: GL1's lines from whoever sits in that seat, CinemaLibrary.resolved), `card` (a title card mid-timeline), `black` (the shot is black) and `sfx_opt` (sounds T-192 provides: played when they exist). `beds` are the scene's loops [[t, key, db, out_t]], `beds_opt` the optional ones. `hooks` say where each plays in a match (LazarusCinema.plan), `gallery` is the Archive's list, `cast` the people's looks (CinemaPerson), `risen_kind` the key the risen are built from (CinemaRisen.make: T-192's seam). Cards and captions are Latin letters only; the Cyrillic is paint on the props.

lazarus_saturday._what: The prologue: Chetverodnevo, Lazarus Saturday, 12 April 1930 (docs/CUTSCENES_LAZARUS.md §1).

shots._what: Black. Far off, a single feast bell; rooks.

card.title: CHETVERODNEVO
card.subtitle: a village a long day's cart from the district town

shots._what: Grey light, a thaw. A rutted road of brown water, snow in the ditches, the wooden church and its tent-roofed bell tower at the end of it. Smoke from one chimney.
The villagers kneeling in the road, in a loose band across it: old men with their caps off, women in shawls, children held by the shoulders. Nobody speaks. The bell.

From the church porch, the long lens down the road over the kneeling heads: the truck, an AMO-F-15, canvas back, two plain red cloths on poles, people standing in the back. It comes slowly, slithering in the ruts.

Alongside the truck as it stops short of the kneeling line. The brigade climbs down: town coats, caps, red armbands of plain cloth, crowbars, rope, a tin speaking trumpet. Last, from the cab, Volkov. He looks at the kneeling road and then, quickly, away from it. The bell stops mid-swing.

The church door from the road, the kneeling backs out of focus in the foreground. The speaking trumpet reads the slogans, flat, off a paper. On the door, in a black cassock and skufia, the keys in his hand: Father Serafim. Out of focus behind him the people in the road get up and are walked to its edge; the camera holds on Serafim and never racks to them (nobody is struck on screen; the sound carries it).
Serafim, close. He raises his free hand, palm down, toward the road behind the camera: get up, go home.
Volkov on the step below him with a paper, over his shoulder onto Serafim. Correct, formal, twenty-six, his voice a touch too loud.
The reverse, over Serafim's shoulder onto Volkov. Serafim's hand closes on the keys: not a fist. He simply doesn't open it.
Low at the step, the two of them small against the door, the brigade head's boots entering frame. Volkov turns to him and keeps his voice down. He is managing it.
The ring of keys in Serafim's hand at the end of a quiet shot. Two of the brigade step into frame from either side. Cut on the first movement.
Black. Over black, the sound: a grunt, cloth, the keys hitting the boards. 'Lord, have mercy.'

Daylight again. A rope goes up to the bell. Two men on the belfry rail work a crowbar at the yoke. Below, out of focus, Serafim on his knees between two of the brigade, not held now, just kept there. He is praying.
From the ground, looking up: the bell swings out over the rail on the rope. The rope runs. The bell drops.
At ground level on the mud where it lands: the bell cracks, one dead note and a seam opening up its waist. Mud on the bronze.
From far down the road, the long lens, the tower centre frame, the brigade running out of the porch. A whistle. The road is cleared back.
The same frame: the tower comes down. The charge takes the base, the shingled tent roof leans, folds and goes, slowly, in a plume of grey dust that rolls up the road toward the camera.

Through the thinning dust: the church still standing, a raw stump where the tower was. Serafim on his knees in the road, coughing. Volkov by the truck, writing on a board. He looks up at Serafim and, for a moment, looks ashamed.

Inside, under the floor: a stone undercroft older than the church over it, down the steps behind two lanterns. A low door at the bottom and over it a lamp still lit on its chain, a small flame in red glass; over the door, cut in the stone, the line in Church Slavonic.
The letters, close. Volkov's lantern comes up to read them. Behind him on the stair, allowed down to see what they do, Serafim reads it first, from memory, in the old tongue.

The crypt: a vaulted room the size of a kitchen, a stone altar step, nothing on the walls. On the step, alone, a small vessel: dark metal, a wax seal gone grey, a cord. No silver anywhere. The brigade fill the door and go quiet.
Serafim in the doorway between two brigade men, not pleading: asking. He uses the young man's first name as a priest would.
His hands and the vessel on the step: the knife under the wax, the wax lifts in one grey curl; the cord; the lid.

Close on the vessel's mouth in the lantern's light, held: the blood is still wet. It moves when the lantern shakes, catching the light the way only something wet does. [gore: full, red and a drop runs down the lip; low, red; off, only dark and wet]
The room, Volkov standing up too fast. He recovers in front of the brigade. The clever answer. His voice is wrong.
Serafim in the door; the men move past him. He has stopped asking. He says it to nobody, flat, like a doctor giving a date.
Black. Silence. The card.

The mortuary room off the fever ward in the district town (respect review R-03): a cold whitewashed room where the dead wait for the cart, plank trestles, three bodies at the near end with sheets drawn up over the faces, the open door to the ward at the far end and a nurse in a white kerchief in it with her back to us. A tag on a nail: 18.IV. On the nearest sheet a bandaged hand lies outside the cover.

The nearest sheet, held. The sheet moves, once, at the chest, as if someone under it had drawn breath. Then the bandaged hand turns over. Cut before anything sits up. [gore: full, a stain spreads at the hand]

A late snow has turned the thaw back. The OGPU cordon: men in greatcoats and winter helmets, rifles slung, forty metres apart, their backs to us; a field telephone on a post; a fire in a drum. At the end of the road Chetverodnevo burns, the church's stump black against it. Figures move in the fire's light far off, walking. We cannot tell whose.

The church door, shut, a lantern on it. Nailed over it, a painted board: TIF · KARANTIN · VKHOD VOSPRESHCHYON (in Cyrillic, paint on the board). A hammer's last blows. Below it, on its nail, the key ring, untouched.
A Moscow train. Volkov on the bench, upright, a grey lead case on his knees and both arms around it. His cap off. Snow going by the window. He is not asleep and will not be.
The same road in late spring from the same place: grass, no church, no tower, no houses, a few blackened timbers in the nettles. Nothing stands. The rooks.
Black. The card. The chant ends on its held note.

card.title: Chetverodnevo is not on any map.

fourth_day._what: East Prussia, the East Prussian line, October 1944; four days later, the field grave and the road west (§2).

shots._what: Black. Rain.

card.title: EAST PRUSSIA
card.subtitle: the East Prussian line · the German line

shots._what: Rain, mud, a German line: a trench of brown water, a sandbagged MG position under a tarpaulin, a field telephone wire, a church spire with no roof far off in the rain, a dead horse in the wire (no close-up). Helmets move under the parapet. No faces close.

The Soviet observation post: a dugout roofed with logs, a trench periscope, a field telephone, a map in oilcloth. Two officers of the division with binoculars. Between them, not looking through anything, Volkov, his hands in his cape. The telephone.
The handset in Volkov's hand, his face in the slit's light behind. He gives it to the colonel without a word. The colonel's order is HQ's.

The long lens from the Soviet side onto the German trench. The salvo. The shells hit and don't explode properly: no fireball, no splinters. Each opens like a seed pod in a low, dirty brown puff that lies down in the rain instead of rising.
Volkov and the colonel at the slit. The colonel lowers the binoculars and asks with his face. Volkov answers without taking his eyes off the trench.
Black, the rain continuing under it, then silence. The card.

Morning, no rain, low cloud. A field grave: a row of mounds behind an aid station's tents, a wooden pyramid marker on each with a tin star and a pencilled name under a scrap of glass, a shovel still in the heap. Red Army soldiers at a field kitchen with their backs to it.

Low on one mound, the marker in frame: the earth moves. A clod rolls. A ridge rises along the mound's spine and the marker leans. The soldiers behind, one by one, turn to look at it. Nobody reaches for a rifle. Not yet.
Their faces. Boys. One takes off his cap. One crosses himself and looks round to see who saw. The sergeant's hand goes to his rifle sling and stops there.
The set on the kitchen's cart, its whip aerial against the low cloud. HQ answers.

The last shot: a long line of the risen walking west in greatcoats past their own guns. Dozens, in the road and beside it, greatcoats stiff and white with frost, some bareheaded, boots missing, walking the way men walk who are very tired. The crews stand off and let them pass. Nobody shoots.
Black. The chant's held note.

staub._what: Kaltenbrunn, 20 December 1944: the dust mill on the night of the Erwachen (§3).

shots._what: Black. The mill under it.

The violet powder: a fine dust sliding down a glass-fronted sifter into a hopper, lit from inside the machine, so fine it hangs. Men in rubber masks and gauntlets at the hopper. A canister under it fills. Nothing on the walls but the Wiederkehr mark and a lot number board.

Reinholt at the gauges: a bank of three dials (fineness, resonance, temperature) and a clock. A white coat over her dress, hair pinned, a pencil. She watches the gauges, not the men. The resonance needle sits high. She writes a number.

Outside, in the snow, under floodlights: the canisters loaded onto rockets aimed east. Six squat rockets on a rail frame, each with a steel canister clamped under its nose, a crew in winter whites; the rail points at the black line of hills.

The weather station: the hut's lit window on the hill, the anemometer's cups and the wind vane in silhouette on its mast against the valley's lights: Kaltenbrunn village, Wilcza Gora across it, a dozen farms, the lamp at the crossroads far north-west.
The launch, seen from the hill: six streaks going east over the hills, low, their exhaust lighting the snow. The crews watch them go.
The wind vane, held. The cups slow, stop, and start the other way. The vane swings: a quarter turn, a hesitation, then round, until it points west. The cups race.

The dust coming back over the hills: on the eastern ridge a violet haze, lit from inside by nothing, rolls down toward the valley like a slow wave, and the lights of the villages go out one by one as it reaches them. The plant's floods are the last lights left.

That same night: Reinholt alone at the Heart's console in the Core Vault, her hand turning the resonance to its stop, the pencil still behind her ear, her face lit from below. She is not looking at the gauges now.
Black. The hum climbs and stops.

gravelight_one._what: Inside the C-47 over the front at night, 23 December 1944, 23:10 to 23:41: Map 0's crash, rebuilt (§4).

shots._what: Black; engines.

card.title: GRAVELIGHT ONE
card.subtitle: a C-47 out of Brindisi · over the Silesian front

shots._what: Inside the C-47: bucket seats along both walls, the static line, cargo lashed under a net, a red dome lamp, frost on the inside of the skin. The four passengers strapped in on the port side with their kit between their boots. Nobody is talking. One is asleep or pretending.

Through the window, over a passenger's shoulder: flares. The ground 600 m down, snow, black woods, a river. White parachute flares hang over it in a line, and under them columns of figures walking west in the snow, hundreds, in no formation, past gun pits and burning vehicles, and nothing fires at them.

Closer on the window, the glass frosted at the edges, a flare lighting the cabin white for a second. The columns under a flare: greatcoats, bare heads, the walk. Both armies and the dead between them.

From the cockpit doorway over Selwyn's and the co-pilot's shoulders onto the windscreen: the instrument panel's dim red; ahead the dark hills, snow, and a violet light low on the horizon, bearing oh-four-oh, a thread first, then a column.
The four faces along the port wall, lit violet from the starboard windows. One checks a watch. The dome lamp dims.

The panel and Selwyn's hands: the violet column fills the windscreen. The engines die, both at once: the needles fall, the panel's lamps go out, the props windmill. Selwyn's hands do everything right in the dark.

Outside for one shot: the dark aircraft, props turning slowly, no lights, gliding down over a snowfield with the violet column behind it. Ahead and below, a crossroads, a stable, and the inn's lit windows, every one of them warm, the only lamplight for miles.

The cabin from the floor: boots, hands on the seat frames, heads down, the net straining. The crash: the first touch, the second, the floor jumps, the lamp goes, cargo breaks loose across the frame, the picture whites out in snow through a torn skin.
Black. Ringing silence, then the small sounds come back: a fire starting, a ticking, the wind.
Black into the inn opening.

epilogue_1953._what: After KÜNDIGUNG and its credits (MAP4_FERNFLUG.md §12.11, cards_m4.json cards.moscow53): not voiced, dread, not a sequel advert (§5).

shots._what: Black. A vault's silence; a ventilation fan far off.

A steel shelf in a concrete vault, one bulb in a cage. On it the grey lead case from the train, its paint worn to the metal at the corners. An old man's hand rests on it: liver spots, a signet ring, the cuff of a good suit, no uniform. The hand does not lift. The fingers tighten once, as if the case had moved.

caption.text: A lead case on a steel table. An old man's hand resting on it. The hand is forty-nine years old and looks older. It opened this case once before, on an altar step, to prove there was nothing in it.

shots._what: Black. The note dies.
Black. The second card, after the first has gone.
